text.title: Orchestrator Token Protocol Rules
text.summary: Six testable rules that make a fan-out pay for retrieval once. R1 removes the duplicate scans; R4 is the checkpoint that keeps the other five from silently regressing.

rule.statement: The orchestrator MUST perform the search the fan-out needs and pass the resulting identifiers to subagents. A subagent brief MUST NOT contain a search query for content the parent has already located. Where a child must search — genuinely disjoint exploration — that MUST be stated in the brief as a deliberate exception, not left as the default.
rule.rationale: Two full product builds were run under a meter. The CLI-first pipeline issued 22 `faion search` calls and wrote 8,669,708 cache-write tokens against 150 input and 9,200 output tokens: each fresh subprocess re-sent the whole candidate manifest to the provider. At 2026-08 Opus rates that is roughly $55 for 22 searches, about $2.50 each — enough to erase the pipeline's entire measured saving elsewhere and leave it 5-6x more expensive overall. The searches were near-duplicates; one search shared as identifiers would have cost one.

rule.statement: A subagent brief MUST reference content by stable identifier — hash-ID or path — and MUST NOT embed the body. Pasting a retrieved document into a brief is FORBIDDEN, including excerpts assembled "to save the child a call".
rule.rationale: A body pasted into a brief is paid once per child and again on every turn that child re-sends its context, so an N-way fan-out multiplies it by more than N. An identifier is a few tokens and lets the child fetch only if it actually needs the text — which, for most fan-outs, most children do not.

rule.statement: Subagents MUST hydrate with the sink form of the content fetch — `faion get-content ID --sink` — which writes the body to disk and returns a short receipt. Piping a body through stdout into a prompt is permitted ONLY when the consumer is a human reading a terminal.
rule.rationale: The sink form returns a roughly 30-token receipt naming the file it wrote; the body reaches the agent as a file it may read, in part, on demand. Stdout transit puts the whole document into the context permanently and unconditionally, so the agent pays full price for a document it may only need one section of. Batch fetches take the same flag and return N receipts in one doc-set.

rule.statement: The orchestrator MUST record a meter snapshot immediately before the fan-out and immediately after it rejoins, and MUST report the delta alongside the agent-visible token count. A pipeline that reports only agent-visible tokens MUST NOT claim a saving.
rule.rationale: The 2026-08-09 experiment reported minus 3.4% agent-visible tokens while being several times more expensive in reality, because the CLI's own provider calls happened inside child processes and appeared in nobody's context. The delta between two `faion tokens report` snapshots is the only number that includes them. Without the brackets the protocol's own effect is unfalsifiable.

rule.statement: Every spawned child process MUST set `FAION_SUBAGENT=1` in its environment. The orchestrator MUST set it as part of the spawn, not delegate it to the child's own prompt.
rule.rationale: The flag does two things at once. It drops the conversation-transcript block, which the child does not have and would otherwise pay to inject. And because the cache key includes the transcript hash, every no-transcript caller lands in one shared bucket keyed only by query, tier and corpus hash — so a repeat of an identical query from a different OS process is served from cache with zero provider calls. Left unset, each child hashes a different transcript, misses, and pays full price for a search its sibling already ran. A flag the child is merely told to set is a flag that gets forgotten in exactly the deep fan-outs where it matters most.

rule.statement: Non-interactive callers MUST request the narrow output form — `--terse` and, when only identifiers are consumed downstream, `--output ids`. Prose or full-document output MUST NOT be parsed by a pipeline stage.
rule.rationale: Rendered output carries framing, summaries and formatting sized for a human reader, all of which enters the consuming agent's context and none of which survives parsing. Where the next stage needs a list of identifiers, every other byte is waste that a flag removes.
